title: v0.4.23 integration: Core-compatible enrollment/session fixtures and real remote Docker/Podman acceptance
author: mcpdev80
body:
Parent release: mcpdev80/baseharbor#571 (v0.4.23). Baseline: released Core `1aa1a503facc1f4cbbd58fab21619fda53ed6d47`; Console main `0d7c8522ef91f0fc5af47cf6123868f73f543ed4`; Node Connector main `572b81dab1e48ef7df18c4e40b038ba33e196827`. Re-fetch heads at implementation start.

Pre-freeze rule: no legacy compatibility, migration layer or obsolete aliases. Native standards first; preserve shared Core authorization, policy, ownership and secret safety. 
Follow-up to closed #1 and merged #2, not a second connector/control plane. Coordinate with Core remote-access and CI children of #571.

## Work
- Align current targetaccess wire/session/bootstrap/stream definitions with the canonical versioned Core package/fixtures. Keep descriptor versus transport distinctions explicit and detect drift automatically.
- Complete integration with real Core enrollment/CA authority and outbound session admission; confirm identity, Target/runtime binding, version/capability negotiation, nonce/one-time token and trusted destination checks.
- Validate actual remote Docker Compose and rootless Podman Quadlet staging/apply/status/logs/metrics/container exec/PTY/destroy through Core; Connector never authorizes/selects placement or owns desired state.
- Verify request freshness/replay/idempotency boundaries for mutating operations, audit correlation, timeout/cancellation and bounded concurrent streams/control.
- Test renewal/rotation/CA overlap/revocation on new and active sessions; document exact revalidation bounds and fail-closed behavior.
- Preserve at-least-once log reconnect/replay with expired-cursor errors; PTY disconnect cannot silently resume another process.
- Test wrong peer/Target/runtime, rejected enrollment, unavailable Core, interrupted transfer, path/symlink escape, foreign-resource preservation and cleanup.
- Refresh README/TARGET-ACCESS/DEPLOYMENT docs to distinguish connector-side completed features from end-to-end supported operation. Windows cross-build is not terminal/runtime support.
- No mandatory connector for native Kubernetes/OpenShift, no inbound management endpoint, no generic shell or private-source publication.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Shared golden fixtures + package tests/vet/build pass locally/HF first.
- [ ] Real pinned Core -> Connector -> Docker and Podman gates pass with ownership/cleanup proof.
- [ ] Enrollment/reconnect/rotation/revocation/stream negative cases are executable and retained as evidence.
- [ ] Effective capabilities derive from authenticated runtime, not static promises.
- [ ] Documentation and evidence correctly separate unit/fixture, cross-build and live runtime support.


## v0.4.23 coordinated implementation — 2026-10-06
Core release umbrella: mcpdev80/baseharbor#571. Public contract/governance: #805; configuration/policy: #609; browser/terminal: #806; Core connector authority/transport: #807; additive pinned CI/evidence: #808 (all in mcpdev80/baseharbor). Implement against canonical Core wire fixtures and exact immutable revisions; do not wait on the already closed #767/#768/#769/#770 foundations. Distinguish delivered contract foundation from required live integration. Update docs/contract-readiness and source/CI checks before final coordinated prerelease.

comments.author: mcpdev80
comments.body: Private Draft #4 now includes `46e9d269a59716c99a0379d553a399864f479c61`: enrollment installation requires a client-only leaf, expected URI and local key, exact expiry, strict single-certificate/CSR PEM and CA-only trust bundles. Negative tests reject server/dual-purpose leaves, added PEM material and wrong validity before writing identity files. Complete `go test -race ./...`, `go vet ./...` and the CLI source build passed (the materialized checkout uses `-buildvcs=false`). Core endpoint/wire/session/lifecycle integration remains pending; these are source checks, not remote runtime or acceptance evidence.

comments.author: mcpdev80
comments.body:
Public-repository hygiene/alignment completed on 2026-10-07:

- Apache-2.0 LICENSE added.
- SECURITY.md added with Connector-specific fail-closed/authority boundaries.
- Standard public CI added: `go test ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and connector build.
- README now exposes local validation and states explicitly that package/CI success is not end-to-end support evidence.
- Existing tests were confirmed present across fssecure, targetaccess, connector, capability and runtime adapter packages; the earlier "no visible tests" impression was a code-search/indexing false negative.

Historical commits were intentionally not rewritten: exact SHAs/evidence remain more valuable than cosmetic history cleanup.

End-to-end release acceptance remains this issue's pinned Core -> Connector -> Docker/Podman evidence, not the repository-local quality gate.

comments.author: mcpdev80
comments.body: 2026-10-08 additional acceptance requirements (planning only; NO implementation requested): User is blocked by manual Connector setup. Desired flow is `baha node add` on Core (name, runtime, one-time short-lived token) then `baha node connect` on remote Podman/Docker host (Core URL + secure token prompt), automatically detect runtime, install/configure/launch rootless connector service, enroll locally generated key via pinned/trusted Core identity, verify mTLS, establish outbound-only persistent connection and report READY. Core/CLI owns user-facing `baha` commands and authorizations; connector repository owns executable packaging, runtime/service lifecycle integration, secure bootstrap and renewal/reconnect behavior; preserve separate minimal Target Access boundary. Provide safe installation/update/uninstall paths (no Go required on node), systemd user/lingering behavior on rootless Podman, idempotent repeat enrollment with explicit re-enroll/revocation policy, actionable diagnostics, no default insecure TLS/token in argv/shell history/logs, no secrets exposed. `baha node list/status` must show observed liveness, trust/cert expiry/capabilities and disconnected reason. Test E2E Core Docker VM 192.168.6.166 to remote Podman VM 192.168.6.148, independent remote Target `podman-node-test`, preserving existing `podman-test` Core/containers. Cover first enroll, restart, certificate renew, Core unavailable/reconnect, invalid/expired/used token, revoked certificate, tenant mismatch, unsupported runtime, remote resource list/inspect and no silent local fallback. Current README documents manual binary startup, bootstrap URL/CA/token-file, identities and session pool; those primitives exist, but seamless guided lifecycle is NOT proven. Coordinate with baseharbor#769, baseharbor#807, and Console #2; do not mark shipped without pinned cross-repo runtime evidence.
